title: Amazon yeni Kindle ailesini tanıttı: Daha ince tasarım ve hız
summary: Amazon, Kindle serisini yenileyerek daha hafif tasarımlar, alüminyum gövde seçenekleri ve Bluetooth sayfa çevirme kumandası gibi yeni aksesuarlar tanıttı.
body:
Amazon, popüler e-kitap okuyucu ailesi Kindle serisini yenileyerek daha ince tasarımlar, yeni ekran teknolojileri ve ilk kez sunulan alüminyum gövde seçenekleriyle güncelledi. TechCrunch'ın aktardığına göre şirket, cihazların etrafındaki çıkıntılı çerçeveyi kaldırarak düz ekran tasarımına geçti ve yanlış dokunmaları önlemek için dokunmatik hassasiyeti yeniden düzenledi. Temel Kindle modeli, şirketin açıklamasına göre kitapları yüzde 30 daha hızlı açıyor ve 149,99 dolardan başlayan fiyatlarla satışa sunuluyor.

## Yenilenen Paperwhite ve renkli ekran

Standart modelin yanı sıra Kindle Paperwhite ve renkli ekranlı Kindle Colorsoft da daha ince ve hafif gövdelere kavuştu. Paperwhite, yüksek kontrast oranı ve su geçirmezlik özellikleriyle gelirken, depolama alanını artıran ve dock şarj desteği sunan Signature sürümü de bulunuyor. Paperwhite 199,99 dolardan, Signature sürümü ise 249,99 dolardan başlayan fiyatlarla alıcı buluyor. Kindle Colorsoft ise renkleri daha doğal hissettiren geliştirilmiş ekranıyla 289,99 dolardan satışa çıkarken, Signature sürümü 319,99 dolara mal oluyor. Ayrıca tüm modellerin çocuklara özel sanatçı tasarımı kılıflar ve bir yıllık Amazon Kids+ aboneliği içeren Kids versiyonları da ürün yelpazesine eklendi.

## Yeni aksesuarlar ve sayfa çevirme kumandası

Amazon bu güncellemeyle birlikte ilk kez Kindle serisine yönelik aksesuarlar da tanıttı. Eller serbest okuma imkanı sunan ve Bluetooth ile çalışan Kindle Click kumandası 34,99 dolardan satışa sunulurken, manyetik sayfa çevirme kılıfları ve şarj stantları da aksesuar seçenekleri arasında yer alıyor.

**Neden önemli?** Bu yenileme, Kindle serisinin son yıllardaki en kapsamlı fiziksel değişimi temsil ederken, alüminyum gövde ve kablosuz sayfa çevirici gibi ilk kez sunulan özelliklerle e-kitap okuma deneyimini genişletiyor.

source_texts.title: Amazon just dramatically changed its Kindle lineup with new looks, colors, and more
source_texts.summary: A new pocket-sized e-reader, kid's versions, and Kindle accessories are now available.
source_texts.text:
Amazon's Kindle is synonymous with the e-reader, operating as one of its most well-known and popular products for over a decade. It's such a simple yet effective device, so much so that Amazon has long been desperately trying to upgrade it in order to get people to buy new ones. Most people only need a basic e-readerthat looks good and holds books, but new features keep coming out that you may or may not need on your reading journey in order to entice you into buying another Kindle.
Today, Amazon announced some major changes to its popular line of e-readers as it looks to generate some excitement ahead of the holiday shopping season. There are new versions of each of its Kindles as well as some first-of-their-kind e-reader accessories. Here's everything you need to know about this big announcement.
A new pocket-sized Kindle is now available
The basic model is smaller and lighter
The first big change to the Kindle lineup involves the standard Kindle. The new Kindle is notable due to its size: it now boasts a 6-inch display, making it a more convenient e-reader to carry around, perhaps in your back pocket. So, while there is a lack of actual paperbacks as companies have halted production of the beloved pocket-sized physical books, at least now they are now being replaced by a digital version.
This Kindle boasts 16GB of storage and a battery that can last for up to six weeks, as well as a flush-front design. Amazon also notes that it opens books 30% faster, which I'm not sure I ever really thought about or can really comprehend. You can also opt for this Kindle with an aluminum back, lending a more stable feel to the e-reader.
The Kindle is available starting at $149.99. It comes in Ube and Graphite, which I'm told are colors.
The Kindle Paperwhite and Colorsoft are getting an upgrade
Improved displays and thinner designs
Amazon is also introducing a new Paperwhite, thinner and lighter than previous versions, with waterproofing and an adjustable warm light. It will come with a higher contrast ratio in addition to a battery can go for 12 weeks. You can opt for a Signature edition of the Paperwhite, which offers more storage, and auto-adjusting front light, and dock charging.
The Paperwhite is available starting at $199.99 while the Signature version starts from $249.99.
Meanwhile, the Kindle Colorsoft is being upgraded with a supposedly better display that makes colors feel more natural and lifelike while maintaining brightness that doesn't wash out any images. The display removes glare and seeks to create a uniform look across the entirety of the screen regardless of ambient light. There is also a Signature Edition available that welcomes the same features as the Paperwhite Signature.
The Colorsoft is available starting at $289.99 with the Signature Edition starting from $319.99.
Kids can enjoy their own Kindle, too
Amazon is appealing to young readers with child e-readers
Each of these three Kindles will be available in a Kids version. Amazon boasts that the Kids model features "kid-friendly covers designed by real artists," which I'm curious to see in physical form. A purchase also comes with 12 months free of Amazon Kids+, which is Amazon's collection of games, videos, and books for children.
It's not clear if there are any notable physical or technological differences in the Kids version. Or if the free service for one year is truly worth it. The subscription and the cover seem like the main differences.
These Kids Kindles start at $179.99.
Amazon is introducing Kindle accessories
Extras designed to make Kindles more convenient
Perhaps the most curious part of this announcement is a batch of Kindle accessories that are now available, marking the first time Amazon has sought to create add-ons and extras with its e-reader lineup. In all, there are four new products that you can purchase to enhance your reading experience.
There is the Kindle Click, a small Bluetooth remote that allows you to turn the page of your Kindle when it's not convenient for you to touch the screen. This seems like it will be helpful in very specific circumstances, and I'm not yet sold on it. The Click retails for $34.99. There is also the Page-Turn Cover, a magnetic cover with physical buttons allowing to turn the page. Again, I need to see this in practice to see if it's worth it. This accessory works with the Signature versions of the Paperwhite and Colorsoft, and costs $79.99.
Amazon is also introducing a charging dock that is basically a stand for your Kindle that charges it as you use it. After boasting about how long the batteries last in these devices, I'm not sure if this dock is exactly worth it. This costs $59.99. Lastly, Amazon is welcoming a new line of covers available in knit-fabric, plant-based leather, and pebble premium leather. These covers are designed to be seamless and match colors across the lineup. Covers start at $39.99.
All these new products are now available.

source_texts.title: Amazon's Kindle just got a major upgrade: faster speeds, aluminum shell, and a long-awaited page turner
source_texts.summary: Amazon has given the Kindle line a major refresh , updating all three of the commerce giant's e-readers.
source_texts.text:
Amazon has given the Kindle line a major refresh, updating all three of the commerce giant's e-readers.
It's the basic Kindle and the Paperwhite that get the bulk of the changes this time around, but no matter which device you prefer out of the Kindle, Paperwhite, and Colorsoft, you'll be able to pick up a new aluminum version.
But that's not all, as Amazon has also released some exciting new accessories to complement your new e-reader, including the much awaited page turner.
The basic Kindle gets the biggest upgrades
The basic Kindle now has a less basic build
It's been a few years since we saw the basic Kindle get an update, and the state of the tech market has changed a lot since then. We've seen price rises across all tech, pushed up by an inflating AI bubble, as well as the rise of the tiny e-reader, like the Boox Picco and Xteink X4 Pro.
So how has Amazon risen to the challenge posed by this new world? By snazzing up the Kindle, of course.
The
As mentioned, the basic Kindle is getting the most upgrades from this new range. It's getting an aluminum version, but it's seemingly also getting an upgraded processor, as Amazon mentions it opens books 30% faster than before. Given how sluggish the last Kindle was, this will be a big improvement.
It's also getting a new screen that sits flush with the chassis. Previous Kindles had a significant drop between the shell and the display, and that made it harder to touch the very edge of the display. The new screen means that will be less of a problem.
The Kindle and Kindle Aluminum both release today, October 1. The basic Kindle comes in two new colors, Ube purple and Graphite, and it costs $150 for the ad-supported model, or $170 for the ad-free version.
The Aluminum version costs $190, but doesn't come with any ads. It does come in either Alpine Sky Aluminum or Seaglass Green Aluminum, and it also comes with a magnetic cover attachment.
The Paperwhite and Colorsoft also get some upgrades
But expect to pay for them
The Paperwhite gets similar upgrades, including a flush display, as well as its customary waterproofing. The Signature returns as well, with an adaptive front light, and 32GB of storage. It's only the Signature that gets the aluminum shell, unfortunately.
The Colorsoft hasn't been left out either. Amazon's most expensive small e-reader is back again, though it doesn't get much outside of a potentially improved flush display. Like the Paperwhite, you'll need to stump up for the Signature if you want aluminum, but you do get an automatically adjusting front light to sweeten the deal, as well as a feature to double-tap to turn book pages.
The Paperwhite and Colorsoft are more expensive, as expected. The basic Paperwhite costs $200, or $220 for the ad-free version, while the aluminum Signature costs $250. The Colorsoft is the most expensive, starting at $290 for an ad-free experience. The Signature in aluminum takes that price up to a hefty $320.
The Paperwhite and Colorsoft Kindles are not available until October 28, which includes any of the Signature versions too.
New Kids versions for all three
Catching up to the pack, still great value
All three also come with a Kids version, with kid-friendly covers designed by real artists. Every purchase of a Kids Kindle comes with 12 months of Amazon Kids+ for free access to thousands of books and audiobooks. Prices for those fall between $180 and $300, depending on which model you pick.
There are also some new accessories to choose from when picking your new Kindle.
The most exciting of the bunch is the new page turner, the Kindle Click. It's pretty much as you'd expect — a long handle with a pair of buttons to turn pages back and forth. It's useful for anyone who doesn't hold their Kindle while reading. It can be used with any of the new Kindles, and any Kindle from 2024 onwards. It costs $35.
There's also a magnetic charging stand compatible with the Signature models of the Paperwhite and Colorsoft. It costs $60.
More exciting for those models, though, are the Page-Turn covers. These attach magnetically to the device's pogo pins, and come with physical page turn buttons, though come with the higher price of $80.
Finally, there are also a bunch of new standard cases, available in knit fabric, plant-based leather, and pebbled premium leather, as well as magnetic covers for aluminum Kindles. Those cost $40 each.

source_texts.title: The new Kindle ditches the bezel in a push toward a smaller, lighter e-reader
source_texts.summary: The new Kindle lineup features its lightest and thinnest designs yet, with a sleek, front-flush display that eliminates bezels for good.
source_texts.text:
Amazon is giving the Kindle its most significant physical redesign in years, introducing a refreshed lineup of e-readers built around a deceptively simple idea: getting rid of the bezel.
The redesigned Kindle unveiled Thursday replaces the traditional raised bezel surrounding the display with a flush-front design, creating a cleaner, more seamless look. But bezels also give readers a place to rest their fingers without accidentally touching the screen and triggering a page turn or another touchscreen command. Amazon says it has designed around that problem.
At a press briefing, Kevin Keith, Amazon’s vice president of devices, said the company is using “Cap” (capacitive) touch technology and haptics to create what he describes as a “dead zone.” As a reader grips the Kindle, the device detects where a finger is resting and adjusts the touch-sensitive area accordingly.
“When you’re gripping the Kindle, wherever you put your thumb, it will self-detect a dead zone in the Cap touch. It will just readjust, and it’ll know that the finger is there,” Keith said.
Alongside the bezel-free redesign, the standard 6-inch Kindle is now 6.8 millimeters thick and weighs 140 grams, making it both thinner and lighter than its predecessor. Amazon is positioning it as the most pocket-friendly Kindle in the lineup.
Amazon said the new display is also 30% faster at page turns than the previous generation. The lineup also introduces new colors, including Ube, Alpine Sky, Seaglass Green, Graphite, and Fig.
The new Kindle starts at $149.99 and is available in Ube and Graphite. For the first time, Amazon is also offering an aluminum-backed version, with 32GB of storage and color options, including Alpine Sky and Seaglass Green.
The redesign extends to the Kindle Paperwhite, which is also thinner and lighter than the previous generation.
Amazon describes the Paperwhite as having the largest display in the Kindle lineup, along with the highest contrast ratio. The company says the combination is designed to deliver “deep blacks and crisp text, and images that pop off the screen, whether you’re reading in bright sunlight or under the covers at night.”
The standard Paperwhite comes with 16GB of storage and costs $199.99 in Graphite. A 32GB Signature Edition costs $249.99 and is available in Graphite and Seaglass Green.
The Kindle Colorsoft, which Amazon introduced in 2024 as its first Kindle with a color display, also adopts the thinner, lighter, flush-front design used across the refreshed lineup. The standard Colorsoft has 16GB of storage and starts at $289.99 in Graphite. A 32GB Signature Edition is available in Graphite and Fig for $319.99.
The new Kindle and its aluminum version are available starting today in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, Brazil, the U.K., Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Ireland, the Netherlands, Belgium, Sweden, Poland, Japan, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Egypt, and Australia.
The new Kindle Paperwhite and Kindle Colorsoft are available for preorder across the same regions.
Amazon is also continuing to offer its Kids lineup. The Kids Kindle is currently available for purchase, whereas the Kids Kindle Colorsoft is available for preorder in the U.S., Canada, the U.K., Germany, and Japan.
